basics.name: Egor Petrov
basics.label: PhD Student in Computer Science, Columbia University
basics.summary: PhD student at Columbia University (DAP Lab), advised by Eugene Wu and Kostis Kaffes. Research on efficient large-scale LLM training: pretraining and post-training, parallelisms, optimization, and scaling laws.

work.name: DAP Lab, Columbia University
work.summary: Advised by Eugene Wu and Kostis Kaffes.
highlights: Studying optimization dynamics in RL post-training (RLVR): benchmarking optimizer behavior and loss-landscape changes relative to pretraining, and their effect on downstream tasks.
Developing staleness-mitigation methods for asynchronous post-training with parallel rollout generation, co-designing algorithms and systems to maximize GPU throughput.

work.name: Yandex Research
highlights: Led research on asynchronous pipeline parallelism for efficient large-scale LLM pretraining; first-author paper accepted to ICML 2026.
Designed and analyzed novel algorithms for distributed training systems, improving scalability and hardware utilization.

work.name: Basic Research in AI Laboratory (BRAIn Lab)
highlights: Pioneered memory-efficient zeroth-order optimization methods for LLM fine-tuning, achieving a 50% reduction in memory footprint (ICML Workshop 2025).
Developed and theoretically analyzed novel stochastic and zeroth-order algorithms for decentralized optimization, validated across multiple domains (UAI 2025, ICLR 2026).
Derived a full second-order (Hessian) characterization of the Transformer block with implications for scaling laws.

work.name: Central University
work.summary: Introduction to AI, Scientific Studio, Python for Data Analysis.
highlights: Held consultations, graded assignments, and mentored student research projects.

work.name: Yandex
work.position: ML Engineer, Personalization Quality R&D Group
highlights: Engineered a production pipeline integrating Vowpal Wabbit-based online features into a large-scale CatBoost model, achieving a 0.1% uplift in core ranking metrics (AUC, nDCG).
Implemented a parallelized, MapReduce-style data converter that accelerated data processing by 20x, reducing model training time from hours to minutes.

work.name: Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (MIPT)
highlights: Held consultations and graded assignments for the Department of Algorithms and Programming Technologies.

projects.name: Rethinking Memory-Efficient Optimizers for LLM Pre-Training
projects.summary: Systematic study of structured optimizer-state compression vs. state quantization under matched memory budgets; peak-memory and communication analysis of optimizer states under sharding (FSDP-style).

projects.name: Hyperparameter Transfer and Scaling Laws for Asynchronous Pretraining
projects.summary: Theoretical and practical transfer rules (learning rate, momentum, batch size, weight decay) and scaling laws in models and tokens for asynchronous pipeline-parallel training; extends our ICML 2026 results.

projects.name: Optimization in RL Post-Training (RLVR)
